stages.restoring: Restoring, and what you will see

apps-and-passcode.body:
Apps are downloaded again from the App Store rather than restored, so the
phone needs the Apple ID password and Wi-Fi, and will look half-empty for a
while. The passcode is not set; set it again.

Saved passwords, Wi-Fi networks and Health data are not there, for the reason
given before any of this started.
apps-and-passcode.title: The phone will finish itself

check-it-worked.body:
Four things, in a minute:

  * The number of conversations looks right.
  * Open the oldest conversation you moved and look at its first message.
    The date should be the one the report said.
  * Names appear rather than phone numbers, in the conversations that had them.
  * Pictures that came across appear as a line of text saying what was sent.
    That is expected: the files themselves are not in the backup.

If any of those is wrong, do not take another backup. The archived one is
still the way back, and taking a backup now is the thing that would spoil it.
check-it-worked.title: Check it actually worked

decline-icloud.body:
When WhatsApp opens it may offer to restore your chat history from iCloud.

Decline it.

Accepting replaces the entire message history — including everything just
merged in — with whatever iCloud happens to hold. This is the single way to
undo the whole exercise in one tap, and it is offered as though it were
helpful.
decline-icloud.expect: WhatsApp opens on the conversation list with the merged history in it.
decline-icloud.title: Say no to restoring chats from iCloud

encryption-off.body:
In Finder, with the phone selected, untick "Encrypt local backup".

It will ask for the password you set a moment ago. This does not remove the
archived backup — that one stays encrypted and stays where it is.
encryption-off.expect: the tick disappears. Finder may start a new backup on its own; let it finish.
encryption-off.title: Turn off encrypted backups

error-211.body:
Find My iPhone was still on. Nothing was written to the phone and nothing has
been lost.

Turn it off and start the restore again.
error-211.title: If the restore stopped with error 211

find-my-back-on.body:
Settings, your name, Find My, Find My iPhone, on.

A phone without it is a phone that cannot be found or wiped if it is lost. It
was turned off for one hour and for one reason, and this is that reason ending.
find-my-back-on.title: Turn Find My iPhone back on

find-my-off.body:
On the phone: Settings, your name at the top, Find My, Find My iPhone, and
turn it off. It asks for the Apple ID password.

A restore with Find My still on stops at the very end with "error 211" and
nothing else. Nothing is written and nothing is lost, but it is an hour spent
for a number instead of a sentence.

Write down that you turned it off. It has to go back on afterwards, and by
then it is easy to forget it was ever off.
find-my-off.expect: the switch goes grey and the phone confirms it.
find-my-off.title: Turn off Find My iPhone

fresh-backup.body:
Back up to this Mac once more. This is the backup that will be changed and
restored, and it must be recent: anything said on the phone after this point
will not be in it and will be gone after the restore.

Say nothing on the phone from here until the restore has finished.
fresh-backup.expect: Finder shows a new date with no padlock beside it.
fresh-backup.title: Back the phone up again, unencrypted this time

go-back.body:
The archived encrypted backup from the first step is the way back, and it is
complete: everything as it was, Health data and passwords included.

In Finder, with the phone selected, choose Restore Backup and pick the
archived one. It will ask for the password set at the start.

Do this before taking any new backup. A new backup does not overwrite an
archived one, but it is not worth finding out otherwise while upset.
go-back.title: Going back

health-data-goes.body:
The backup this restores from has to be unencrypted, because an encrypted one
is sealed with a key that never leaves the phone and nothing on a computer can
open it.

An unencrypted backup does not contain Health data, saved passwords, Wi-Fi
networks, or the keychain. Restoring one means losing those, and there is no
way around it: it is Apple's design, not a limitation of this program.

If Health data matters more than the message history, stop here. The archived
encrypted backup from the previous step still has everything, and restoring
that puts the phone back exactly as it is now.
health-data-goes.expect: nothing yet. This is a decision, not an action.
health-data-goes.title: Know what an unencrypted backup does not carry

looks-stalled.body:
Partway through, the phone shows the Apple logo with a progress bar that does
not move for a long time. This is normal and it is the longest part.

Do not unplug it. Do not hold the power button. A phone interrupted here is a
phone that has to be restored again from the beginning.
looks-stalled.expect:
the bar eventually moves, the phone restarts a second time, and Setup
Assistant appears asking about language and Wi-Fi.
looks-stalled.title: The part that looks like it has frozen

power-and-space.body:
The phone on its cable and the computer on mains power. A restore that is
interrupted by a flat battery is the one way this goes badly wrong.

The computer needs free space for a second copy of the backup, which is as
large as the first.
power-and-space.title: Plug both in, and check there is room

reverify-number.body:
It sometimes asks to verify the number by text message. Keep the SIM in the
phone until this is done, or the message cannot arrive.

Verifying the number does not touch the messages already there.
reverify-number.title: WhatsApp may ask for the phone number again

safety-backup.body:
Connect the phone, open Finder, choose the phone in the sidebar, and back it
up to this Mac with "Encrypt local backup" switched ON. Set a password you
will not lose.

Then right-click that backup in Finder's list and choose Archive.

Archiving is the part people skip and the part that matters. Finder keeps one
backup per phone and writes over it the next time. Without archiving, the very
next backup — the one this process is about to make — replaces the only copy
of everything as it was. Archiving puts it somewhere Finder will leave alone.

Encrypted, because only an encrypted backup carries Health data, saved
passwords and Wi-Fi networks. This is the copy you would go back to.
safety-backup.expect:
the backup appears in Finder's list with a padlock and a date. Check the padlock
is there before going on: no padlock means it was not encrypted, and Health data
and passwords are not in it.
safety-backup.title: Make a safety backup, and archive it

start-restore.body:
In Finder, with the phone selected, choose Restore Backup and pick the one
this program made. Its date is today's.

Nothing you do on the computer from here will change the result. The phone is
being written to; leave it connected and leave it alone.
start-restore.expect: a progress bar on the computer first, then "Restore in progress" on the phone.
start-restore.title: Restore the changed backup

wrong-backup.body:
Finder lists backups by device and date. The changed one is a copy of the
original with today's date, in the same place Finder keeps the rest.

If it is not listed, Finder has not noticed it. Quit Finder and open it again
with the phone connected.
wrong-backup.title: If Finder will not show the changed backup
